item.content:encoded:
The PERIL Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is now accepting applications from young people aged 18 to 24 who want to contribute their perspectives to research on online culture and emerging challenges affecting young people.

The Youth Advisory Council brings together 8–10 young people who meet virtually every two to three months to discuss issues such as online polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging trends in digital culture.

This is a low-lift volunteer opportunity designed to give young people a meaningful voice in research without requiring a major time commitment outside scheduled meetings. Council members bring their lived experiences and perspectives, while PERIL brings its research and expertise. Together, they work toward research and solutions that better reflect the realities facing young people today.

What Is the PERIL Youth Advisory Council?

The Youth Advisory Council (YAC) is an advisory group established by PERIL to ensure that research and proposed solutions are informed by the experiences and perspectives of young people.

The council consists of approximately 8–10 young people between the ages of 18 and 24.

Members meet virtually every 2–3 months and contribute their perspectives on developments in online culture and issues affecting young people.

The council may provide feedback on:

  • Research questions
  • Research findings
  • Proposed solutions
  • Emerging issues and trends
  • Concerns affecting young people
  • How research reflects Gen Z experiences

The goal is to ensure that PERIL’s work is not developed without considering the voices of the people most directly affected by the rapidly changing online environment.

Why the Youth Advisory Council Matters

Young people are among the most active participants in today’s digital environment. Social media platforms, online communities and digital communication increasingly influence how people form relationships, consume information and understand social and political issues.

At the same time, young people may encounter challenges including:

  • Online harassment and abuse
  • Polarization
  • Misogynistic content
  • Extremist content
  • Harmful online communities
  • Stereotyping and discrimination
  • Rapidly emerging online trends
  • Other forms of digital harm

Research into these issues can benefit from the direct perspectives of young people who understand how online culture develops and changes.

The YAC therefore provides an opportunity for young people to contribute directly to research and help ensure that research questions and proposed solutions are relevant to real-world experiences.

What Will Youth Advisory Council Members Do?

Membership is intentionally designed to be a low-lift volunteer role.

Members are not expected to undertake extensive research work outside the meetings.

Instead, participants primarily contribute through their perspectives, discussion and feedback.

Their responsibilities include:

1. Attend Quarterly-Style Virtual Meetings

Members participate in virtual meetings approximately every two to three months.

Meeting schedules are developed collaboratively with members, taking their availability into consideration.

This makes the opportunity suitable for young people who may be studying, working or managing other responsibilities.

2. Share Your Perspective

Members are expected to bring their personal perspectives and experiences to discussions.

This could involve talking about how young people interact with online culture, discussing emerging trends or highlighting concerns that researchers may need to consider.

3. Respond to Research Prompts

During meetings, members may be asked to respond to questions or research prompts.

Participants can provide their thoughts based on their experiences and understanding of issues affecting young people.

4. Provide Feedback on Research

YAC members may review and provide feedback on:

  • Research questions
  • Project findings
  • Proposed solutions
  • Emerging research priorities

Their feedback can help researchers better understand whether their work reflects the realities experienced by young people.

5. Identify Emerging Concerns

Members can help surface issues that may be affecting young people but have not yet received sufficient attention.

This is particularly important in online environments, where trends and communities can develop quickly.

Key Areas of Discussion

The Youth Advisory Council will explore trends in online culture, including several sensitive and rapidly evolving areas.

Online Polarization

Online platforms can contribute to increasingly divided conversations and communities.

YAC members may help researchers understand how polarization appears in young people’s online experiences and how young people perceive these changes.

Online Harms

The council may discuss different forms of harm occurring in digital spaces.

Young people’s perspectives can help identify emerging problems and provide insight into how these experiences affect individuals and communities.

Misogyny

Misogynistic content and communities can have significant effects on online culture.

YAC members can contribute perspectives that help researchers understand how young people encounter and respond to misogynistic ideas and behaviours online.

Extremism

The council may also discuss online extremism and emerging extremist trends.

Young people’s perspectives can help researchers better understand how online environments evolve and how harmful ideas may spread or influence young audiences.

Emerging Online Trends

The scope of the YAC is not limited to the issues currently identified.

The council can also help identify new and emerging concerns affecting young people as online culture continues to change.

What Is the Time Commitment?

One of the key features of this opportunity is its low time commitment.

Members meet virtually approximately every 2–3 months.

Participants are expected to:

  • Attend the scheduled meetings
  • Prepare to contribute their perspectives
  • Respond to research prompts
  • Provide feedback during discussions

There is no expectation that members work on projects outside the meetings.

This makes the council potentially suitable for young people who want to contribute to meaningful research while continuing with university, employment, volunteering or other commitments.

One-Year Membership

YAC members serve for an initial one-year term.

Members have the option to renew their membership once.

Participants may also leave the council at any time. If a member decides to step down, they simply need to inform the team.

This structure provides flexibility while allowing members to contribute meaningfully over an extended period.

Is the Youth Advisory Council Paid?

No.

The YAC is an unpaid volunteer opportunity.

There is no salary or stipend mentioned in the opportunity information.

However, members have the opportunity to contribute directly to research, provide feedback to researchers and help shape work addressing important issues affecting young people.

The experience may also provide an opportunity to develop skills in:

  • Research engagement
  • Communication
  • Critical thinking
  • Giving constructive feedback
  • Advisory participation
  • Understanding online social issues
  • Collaborative discussion

Support for Sensitive Discussions

Some of the topics discussed by the Youth Advisory Council may be sensitive.

These include issues such as online harms, misogyny, extremism and other difficult experiences.

Participation in any particular discussion is entirely voluntary.

Members can choose not to participate in a conversation if they do not feel comfortable discussing a particular subject.

According to the opportunity information, support resources are shared with all members upon joining.

This approach recognises that participants may have different experiences and comfort levels when discussing sensitive topics.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suited to young people who:

  • Are between 18 and 24 years old
  • Have an interest in online culture
  • Want to contribute to research
  • Are interested in issues affecting young people
  • Have perspectives on digital communities and online experiences
  • Want to help researchers better understand Gen Z experiences
  • Can participate in virtual meetings every 2–3 months
  • Are comfortable sharing perspectives and providing constructive feedback

Applicants do not need to be professional researchers.

The purpose of the council is specifically to bring young people’s perspectives and lived experiences into the research process.

How to Apply

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly.

Applicants should apply by email.

Application Email

Applications should be sent to:

perilresearch@american.edu

Email Subject Line

Use the following subject format:

YAC Application First Name Last Name

For example:

YAC Application Jane Smith

What to Include in Your Application

Applicants should provide the following information:

1. First and Last Name

Provide your full name.

2. Age

You should state your current age.

Applicants must fall within the specified 18–24 age range.

3. Location

Provide your city and state.

The supplied opportunity information specifically requests city and state rather than country or continent.

4. Why Are You Interested in Joining the YAC?

Applicants should explain why they want to become a member of the Youth Advisory Council.

The response must be no more than 300 words.

A strong response could explain your interest in:

  • Online culture
  • Youth issues
  • Research
  • Digital communities
  • Online harms
  • Social issues
  • Giving young people a voice
  • Contributing to research and solutions

5. What Do You Hope to Get Out of the Experience?

Applicants should explain what they hope to gain from participating in the council.

This response should also be no more than 300 words.

You might discuss goals such as developing research-related experience, learning from researchers, meeting other young people, contributing to meaningful projects or developing your communication and advisory skills.

6. Resume or CV

Applicants should also attach their resume/CV.

Application Review Process

Applications are reviewed on a quarterly basis.

The process includes:

  1. Submission of the application by email
  2. Review of applications
  3. Shortlisting of candidates
  4. Invitation to a short interview for shortlisted applicants
  5. Selection of Youth Advisory Council members

Because applications are accepted on a rolling basis, interested applicants do not need to wait for a single annual application period.

Is There an Application Deadline?

There is no fixed deadline stated.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly.

This means interested applicants should consider applying as soon as possible rather than waiting for a specific closing date.

Why Join the PERIL Youth Advisory Council?

The YAC offers young people an opportunity to move beyond simply being subjects of research and instead become contributors to the research process.

Members can help researchers understand what matters to young people and how emerging online issues are experienced in everyday life.

The opportunity can provide participants with the chance to:

  • Have their perspectives heard
  • Contribute to research questions
  • Give feedback on research findings
  • Influence proposed solutions
  • Help identify emerging issues
  • Learn about research and advisory work
  • Connect with other young people
  • Contribute to discussions about safer online environments

Perhaps most importantly, members can help ensure that research about young people is informed by young people themselves.

Click HERE  to read more.

Conclusion

The PERIL Youth Advisory Council provides an opportunity for young people aged 18–24 to contribute directly to research examining online culture, polarization, online harms, misogyny, extremism and other emerging issues.

With only virtual meetings every two to three months and no expectation of work outside meetings, the YAC has been intentionally designed as a low-lift volunteer opportunity.

Members serve for one year, with the possibility of one renewal, and can provide meaningful input into research questions, findings, proposed solutions and emerging concerns.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly, giving interested young people the opportunity to apply throughout the year.

For young people who want their experiences and perspectives to play a role in shaping research and conversations about the digital world, the PERIL Youth Advisory Council offers a meaningful way to shape the conversation and advise the research.

Click HERE for more volunteering opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Union for the Mediterranean (UfM) has opened applications for the third edition of the UfM Med Youth Lab, an introductory entrepreneurship and employability skills programme for university students and recent graduates across the Euro-Mediterranean region.

The programme is designed specifically for young people aged 18–29 who are curious about entrepreneurship but have little or no previous experience in the field.

Up to 30 young participants will take part in online training between October and December 2026, followed by practical, in-person workshops in Palermo, Italy, from 14–16 December 2026.

Participation is free of charge, while selected participants from eligible countries will receive financial support covering travel, visa and accommodation costs for the in-person component.

About the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026

The UfM Med Youth Lab is a skills-building initiative organised by the Union for the Mediterranean, with the support of the German Development Cooperation (GIZ) and in partnership with the University of Palermo.

The 2026 edition focuses on introducing young people to foundational concepts in entrepreneurship and employability.

Rather than requiring applicants to already have a business or extensive entrepreneurial experience, the programme specifically targets beginners who want to understand entrepreneurship and develop practical skills they can use in their academic, professional and community activities.

Through expert-led sessions, non-formal education, teamwork and peer learning, participants will develop their entrepreneurial mindset and strengthen practical transferable skills.

What Participants Will Learn

During the programme, participants will develop foundational knowledge and skills in:

  • Entrepreneurial thinking and mindset
  • Innovation
  • Basic financial literacy
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Employability
  • Teamwork and peer learning

The programme is designed to build participants’ confidence and help them understand how entrepreneurial thinking can be applied to real-life challenges.

Training of Trainers Approach

A distinctive feature of the 2026 edition is its Training of Trainers approach.

Participants will receive support to design a simple introductory awareness session about entrepreneurship. They will then be encouraged to share this knowledge with other young people at the national or local level in 2027.

Participants are not expected to become professional entrepreneurship trainers or experts. Instead, the programme aims to equip them with enough knowledge and confidence to act as peer facilitators, introducing basic entrepreneurship concepts within their communities.

This approach allows the impact of the programme to extend beyond the 30 selected participants.

Programme Components

The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 consists of three main components:

1. Online Training

October–December 2026

Selected participants will participate in online learning sessions covering entrepreneurship, innovation, financial literacy, communication and problem-solving.

2. In-Person Workshops

14–16 December 2026

The in-person component will take place in Palermo, Italy.

The workshops will provide participants with opportunities for practical learning, teamwork, peer exchange and interaction with other young people from across the Mediterranean.

3. Follow-Up Activities

2027

Following the main programme, participants will be encouraged to share their newly acquired knowledge through introductory entrepreneurship awareness sessions with peers in their communities.

Who Can Apply?

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Be 18–29 years old at the time of application.
  • Be a national and resident of a UfM Member State.
  • Be currently enrolled in a university programme or have graduated no more than one year before the application deadline.
  • Hold a valid travel document, such as a passport.
  • Have at least B2-level English or equivalent ability to actively participate in discussions and group activities.
  • Have little or no significant previous knowledge, training or professional experience in entrepreneurship.
  • Be fully available to participate in both the online training and the in-person workshops in Palermo.

The programme is specifically designed for beginners.

Applicants with significant previous entrepreneurship training, experience running or funding a start-up, or professional experience working with business-support organisations are not eligible for selection.

Participants from the 2024 and 2025 editions may also apply, provided they meet all eligibility requirements for the 2026 edition.

Eligible Countries

Selected participants from the following countries are eligible for full sponsorship of travel, visa and accommodation expenses associated with the in-person programme:

🇦🇱 Albania
🇩🇿 Algeria
🇧🇦 Bosnia and Herzegovina
🇪🇬 Egypt
🇯🇴 Jordan
🇱🇧 Lebanon
🇱🇾 Libya
🇲🇷 Mauritania
🇲🇪 Montenegro
🇲🇦 Morocco
🇲🇰 North Macedonia
🇵🇸 Palestine
🇸🇾 Syria
🇹🇳 Tunisia
🇹🇷 Türkiye

For selected participants from these countries, travel, visa fees and accommodation for the in-person component in Palermo will be covered.

What Makes This Opportunity Valuable?

The programme provides young people with an opportunity to gain practical entrepreneurship knowledge without requiring them to already have a business idea, start-up or extensive entrepreneurial background.

Participants will also benefit from:

  • Practical entrepreneurship and employability skills
  • Exposure to innovation and entrepreneurial thinking
  • Basic financial literacy
  • Communication and problem-solving skills
  • Peer learning with young people from across the Mediterranean
  • International networking and regional cooperation
  • Hands-on learning in Palermo
  • Experience developing a peer-focused entrepreneurship awareness session

The programme also provides an opportunity for participants to bring what they learn back to their own communities.

Background of the Programme

The UfM Med Youth Lab was first launched in Fes, Morocco, in November 2024.

Its second edition combined online training with in-person workshops in Tirana, Albania, in September and October 2025.

The first two editions focused primarily on project-development skills, helping young people transform ideas into structured project proposals.

Building on lessons from these previous editions, the 2026 programme introduces a new emphasis on entrepreneurship and employability skills, while maintaining the initiative’s focus on practical learning, peer exchange and regional cooperation.

The programme forms part of the UfM’s broader work to strengthen youth participation, skills development and access to opportunities across the Euro-Mediterranean region.

It contributes to the objectives of the UfM Youth Strategy 2030 and the UfM Youth Agenda: Call for Action, which highlight the importance of education, employment, social inclusion and meaningful youth participation.

Application Process

Before applying, candidates should:

  1. Check that they meet all eligibility requirements.
  2. Review the financial coverage available to participants.
  3. Carefully read the application guidelines.
  4. Prepare the required attachments.
  5. Submit the completed application before the deadline.

Application Deadline

📅 30 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST

How to Apply

Interested applicants can submit their applications through the official UfM Med Youth Lab application platform:

🔗 Apply for the UfM Med Youth Lab 2026

For questions or difficulties with the application process, applicants can contact:

medyouthlab@ufmsecretariat.org

Conclusion

The UfM Med Youth Lab 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for university students and recent graduates to gain foundational entrepreneurship and employability skills in an international learning environment.

With free participation, online training, practical workshops in Palermo, and full travel, visa and accommodation support available to selected participants from eligible countries, the programme provides a strong opportunity for young people who are at the beginning of their entrepreneurial journey.

Young people who meet the eligibility requirements and have little or no previous entrepreneurship experience are encouraged to apply before the 30 August 2026 deadline.

Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Commonwealth Youth Council (CYC) has launched One Country, One Project 2026, a Commonwealth-wide initiative designed to recognise and showcase impactful youth-led projects that are responding to real challenges in communities.

The initiative is being launched around International Youth Day 2026, observed annually on 12 August. The United Nations has designated the 2026 theme as “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations,” highlighting the shared aspirations of young people across different countries and communities, including the desire for opportunity, meaningful participation, decent work, dignity and a sustainable future.

What Is One Country, One Project?

One Country, One Project is an initiative of the Commonwealth Youth Council, the official representative body of young people across the Commonwealth’s 56 member states.

According to the CYC, the initiative was developed around a simple principle: global problems require local solutions. The programme seeks to work with National Youth Councils and youth leaders in Commonwealth member countries to identify and support locally designed projects that benefit young people.

For the 2026 call, youth-led organisations across the Commonwealth are invited to register projects that will be implemented between August and September 2026.

This creates an opportunity for organisations that are already working on community challenges—or are ready to implement a project during this period—to bring their work to the attention of a wider Commonwealth audience.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for youth-led organisations across Commonwealth countries.

Organisations should have a project that addresses a genuine challenge within their community and that can be implemented during the designated August–September 2026 period.

The initiative is particularly relevant to youth organisations working on practical community solutions, social development, youth empowerment, employment, education, climate action, innovation, entrepreneurship, inclusion and other issues affecting young people.

The CYC’s broader programme description explains that the initiative will involve collaboration with National Youth Councils and youth leaders in member countries.

What Kind of Projects Are Relevant?

The initiative is focused on impactful, youth-led projects, rather than simply ideas that have not yet been put into practice.

This means organisations should think about projects that can produce a clear and demonstrable benefit within their communities.

Potential examples could include projects addressing:

  • Youth unemployment and employability
  • Entrepreneurship and economic empowerment
  • Education and skills development
  • Climate action and environmental sustainability
  • Digital inclusion and technology
  • Community health and wellbeing
  • Social inclusion and equality
  • Food security and sustainable livelihoods
  • Community development
  • Innovation and locally driven solutions

The important consideration is not simply the size of the project, but the problem it addresses, the people it serves, what is implemented and the impact that can be demonstrated.

Why This Opportunity Matters

Youth-led organisations are often closest to the challenges affecting their communities. They understand local realities and can develop solutions that respond directly to those circumstances.

This approach also fits closely with the focus of International Youth Day 2026, which recognises that young people experience different social, economic and geographic realities while sharing common aspirations. The UN specifically highlights youth innovation and the importance of practical, creative solutions to local and global challenges.

One Country, One Project therefore provides a platform for youth organisations to demonstrate that young people are not only beneficiaries of development programmes but also designers, implementers and leaders of solutions.

Recognition and Commonwealth Best Project Award

Following implementation, projects will be assessed based on their demonstrated impact.

Outstanding projects will receive recognition at the country level and may be considered for the Commonwealth Best Project Award 2026.

This gives participating organisations an opportunity to gain recognition beyond their immediate community and potentially have their work highlighted at a major Commonwealth gathering.

The award is expected to be presented during CHOGM Week in Antigua and Barbuda.

The 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting will take place in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, from 1–4 November 2026. It will bring together representatives from the Commonwealth’s 56 member countries, including government, business, civil society and youth organisations.

Connection to Commonwealth Youth Engagement

The initiative comes at an important time for youth participation within the Commonwealth.

The 2026 Commonwealth Youth Forum (CYF) will also take place in Antigua and Barbuda alongside CHOGM. The forum is intended to provide young people with a platform to address issues affecting them and ensure that youth perspectives contribute to Commonwealth decision-making.

The 2026 Commonwealth Youth Forum is being held under the theme “Investing in Youth Agency – Co-Creating Pathways towards Shared Prosperity.” A 23-member international taskforce has been selected to help shape and deliver the forum.

Against this backdrop, One Country, One Project offers another avenue for youth-led action to be recognised within the wider Commonwealth youth agenda.

How the Selection Process Works

The process begins with project registration.

After registration, participating organisations are expected to implement their projects during August and September 2026. Projects will then be assessed based on the impact they have demonstrated.

For organisations hoping to stand out, it will therefore be important to document their work carefully. Evidence could include the number of people reached, activities completed, outcomes achieved, community feedback, photographs, testimonials, partnerships and other measurable results.

A strong project should be able to clearly answer three questions:

What problem did you address?

What did you do about it?

What changed as a result?

Application Deadline

The deadline to register for One Country, One Project 2026 is 22 August 2026.

Youth-led organisations across Commonwealth member countries are encouraged to review the requirements and register their projects before the deadline.

How to Register

Official project registration page:
Commonwealth Youth Council – Impact Projects

The CYC’s official impact-projects page confirms that One Country, One Project is being developed to support locally designed projects and that the Council intends to work with National Youth Councils on the initiative. (Commonwealth Youth Council)

Conclusion

The Commonwealth Youth Council’s One Country, One Project 2026 is an opportunity for youth-led organisations to turn local action into wider recognition.

Rather than focusing only on ideas, the initiative places emphasis on projects that are implemented and can demonstrate meaningful community impact. For organisations already working on practical solutions to challenges affecting young people, this could be an opportunity to showcase their work on a Commonwealth-wide platform.

With projects scheduled for implementation between August and September 2026, interested organisations should begin preparing immediately and ensure that their proposed project has clear objectives, beneficiaries, activities and measurable outcomes.

The deadline for registration is 22 August 2026.

Discover more opportunities like this on the OFY webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The 2026–2027 Joint WHO African Region/TDR Impact Grants are now accepting applications for implementation research projects focused on addressing regional public health priorities in Africa.

The initiative is jointly launched by the WHO Regional Office for Africa (AFRO) and TDR, the WHO-hosted Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases. It aims to strengthen health research capacity in developing countries while supporting research that can improve the delivery of high-quality and cost-efficient healthcare in resource-poor settings.

About the Impact Grants

The Impact Grants for Regional Priorities support implementation research that can help translate evidence, policies and health interventions into practical solutions that work in real-world settings.

TDR explains that the programme is designed to strengthen the research capacity of individuals and institutions in countries, generate knowledge and implementation strategies that countries can apply, and encourage cooperation between researchers and national and international partners.

The programme has focused on implementation research since 2014, with WHO regional offices working with TDR to identify research priorities relevant to their regions.

Key Objectives

The 2026–2027 call seeks to support public health-oriented implementation research that can contribute to stronger healthcare systems and better health outcomes.

The initiative particularly aims to:

  • Strengthen health research capacity in developing countries.
  • Support researchers and institutions undertaking implementation research.
  • Generate evidence that can improve the implementation of public health interventions.
  • Develop practical and cost-efficient healthcare solutions for resource-poor settings.
  • Support research addressing important regional health priorities.
  • Encourage collaboration between researchers, health institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

TDR’s broader Impact Grants programme supports researchers and public health practitioners, including those working in ministries of health, academic institutions, research institutes, NGOs and professional or civil service organisations involved in relevant health research.

What Is Implementation Research?

Implementation research focuses on understanding how health interventions, programmes, policies and evidence can be effectively put into practice.

Rather than simply asking whether a health intervention works, implementation research can examine questions such as:

  1. How can an effective intervention be delivered successfully in a particular community?
  2. What barriers prevent health programmes from reaching the people who need them?
  3. How can health services become more efficient and affordable?
  4. What approaches can help governments and health institutions implement evidence-based solutions?
  5. How can successful interventions be adapted to different local settings?

This makes implementation research particularly important in settings where resources are limited and health systems must achieve the greatest possible impact with available resources.

Who Can Apply?

This opportunity is intended for health researchers, public health practitioners and relevant institutions in developing countries, particularly those working on implementation research connected to the African Region’s public health priorities.

Potential applicants may include professionals and researchers working through:

  • Universities and academic institutions
  • Research institutes
  • Ministries of Health and public health programmes
  • Tropical and communicable disease control programmes
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Professional societies
  • Civil service organisations involved in relevant health research

TDR states that cooperation between researchers from different institutions, particularly collaboration involving researchers from more than one country, is strongly encouraged.

Geographical eligibility: The call is focused on the WHO African Region, meaning applicants and research activities should meet the specific country and institutional eligibility requirements stated in the official 2026–2027 call documentation.

The information provided for this announcement does not list the individual eligible countries or detailed institutional eligibility criteria, so applicants should consult the official call page before submitting a proposal.

APPLY HERE

Grant Focus

The grants are intended to support public health-oriented implementation research that addresses identified regional priorities.

Projects should therefore demonstrate a clear connection between the proposed research and practical health challenges affecting communities and health systems.

Successful proposals should ideally demonstrate:

  • A clearly defined public health problem.
  • A strong implementation research question.
  • Relevance to regional priorities.
  • Potential to improve health service delivery or public health outcomes.
  • A realistic research methodology.
  • Potential for the findings to be applied by health systems or policymakers.
  • Appropriate institutional capacity and partnerships.

TDR notes that its Impact Grants are intended to produce research findings that can contribute to national strategies and action plans for controlling and treating diseases of poverty.

Application Languages

Applicants can submit their proposals in any of the following languages:

  • English
  • French
  • Portuguese

This provides researchers across the African Region with multiple options for preparing their applications.

How to Apply

Applications must be submitted electronically through the eTDR portal.

Applicants should:

  1. Review the complete call documentation.
  2. Carefully check the eligibility requirements.
  3. Identify a research project that aligns with the stated regional priorities.
  4. Prepare the required proposal and supporting documentation.
  5. Ensure that all required information is complete.
  6. Submit the application through the eTDR portal before the deadline.

Applications should be prepared carefully because competitive grant programmes generally require proposals to clearly demonstrate the relevance, feasibility and potential impact of the proposed research.

Visit HERE to learn about the WHO Africa and TDR Impact Grants 2026–2027

Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting applications is:

15 September 2026 at 17:00 CEST

Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit before the final hours of the deadline to avoid technical problems or incomplete submissions.

Why This Opportunity Matters

The Impact Grants are particularly relevant for researchers who want their work to move beyond academic publication and contribute to real improvements in public health practice.

TDR’s Impact Grants have previously supported implementation research across different regions and have been used to strengthen links between research institutions, healthcare delivery and disease-control programmes.

For African researchers, this type of funding can provide an opportunity to develop locally relevant evidence addressing challenges that may not be adequately captured by research conducted elsewhere.

Conclusion

The 2026–2027 Joint WHO African Region/TDR Impact Grants provide an opportunity for researchers and public health practitioners to develop implementation research addressing important health priorities in the African Region.

The programme combines research capacity strengthening, evidence generation and practical health-system impact, making it particularly relevant to researchers whose work aims to improve how health interventions are delivered in resource-constrained settings.

CIVICUS Global Digital Action Toolkit Consultancy 2026

CIVICUS Global Alliance is seeking an experienced consultant or consultancy team to develop a Global Digital Action Toolkit, a practical resource designed to help activists, civil society organisations, and citizens organise and participate in collective action in digital spaces safely, strategically, and effectively.

The consultancy offers a contract worth up to USD 9,000, inclusive of professional fees, taxes, and other associated costs. The selected consultant will work with CIVICUS to research, design, write, and finalise an approximately 15-page publication addressing digital organising, online mobilisation, digital protection, strategic communications, responsible digital storytelling, and impact measurement.

The consultancy is expected to run for approximately three months, from mid-September to mid-November 2026.

About CIVICUS Global Alliance

CIVICUS is a global alliance focused on defending and strengthening people power and civic action. The organisation brings together more than 17,000 members across more than 180 countries and works to protect civic freedoms, challenge violations, and strengthen the ability of people and civil society organisations to organise effectively.

CIVICUS places particular emphasis on amplifying excluded and marginalised voices, especially those from the Global South.

Through its work, CIVICUS supports efforts to create more accountable, effective, innovative, and inclusive civil society movements around the world.

Background to the Global Digital Action Toolkit

Digital platforms have become an increasingly important space for civic participation, activism, organising, advocacy, and public mobilisation.

Activists and civil society organisations can use digital platforms to communicate with large audiences, coordinate campaigns, build movements, share information, document events, and advocate for social and political change.

However, the growing importance of digital spaces has also created new challenges and risks.

Activists increasingly face threats such as:

  • Digital surveillance
  • Internet shutdowns
  • Disinformation
  • Online harassment
  • Platform restrictions
  • Restrictions on digital communication
  • Risks associated with organising online
  • Challenges related to digital security and privacy

CIVICUS already provides practical guidance for peaceful protest through its Global Protest Guide. However, there is a need for complementary guidance specifically focused on collective action that takes place in digital environments.

The Global Digital Action Toolkit is intended to address this gap.

The toolkit will provide practical guidance that helps activists and citizens understand how to plan and participate in digital assemblies and collective action while considering safety, strategy, communication, mobilisation, and impact.

Purpose of the Consultancy

The main purpose of this consultancy is to research, design, and develop a practical Global Digital Action Toolkit that provides actionable guidance for people organising collective action in digital spaces.

The final resource should be practical rather than purely theoretical. It should combine useful recommendations with real-world examples and tools that activists and civil society organisations can apply in different contexts.

The approximately 15-page publication is expected to include a combination of:

  • Practical recommendations
  • Case studies
  • Examples
  • Checklists
  • Guidance
  • Visual recommendations
  • References
  • Practical approaches to digital organising
  • Information on digital protection and resilience

The toolkit should be suitable for an international audience and recognise that activists operate in very different political, legal, social, and technological environments.

Key Objectives of the Consultancy

The selected consultant or consultancy team will be responsible for achieving several important objectives.

1. Develop practical written content

The consultant will develop the main written content for the Global Digital Action Toolkit.

The content should provide practical guidance that activists and civil society organisations can use when planning or participating in digital collective action.

2. Expand on the Global Protest Guide

The toolkit should complement and expand the scope of CIVICUS’s existing Global Protest Guide.

Rather than duplicating existing guidance, the consultant should identify areas where digital collective action requires additional considerations and provide appropriate guidance.

3. Ensure global relevance

The recommendations should be relevant to activists and civil society organisations operating across different regions of the world.

The toolkit should recognise that digital organising can take place under very different conditions, including environments with:

  • Strong civic freedoms
  • Restricted civic space
  • Internet shutdowns
  • Government surveillance
  • Platform restrictions
  • Different legal frameworks
  • Different levels of technological access
  • Different levels of digital literacy

4. Make the toolkit practical and accessible

The final publication should be easy for its intended users to understand and apply.

The consultant should avoid creating a resource that is overly academic or theoretical. Instead, the toolkit should translate research and experience into clear recommendations and practical tools.

Scope of Work

The successful consultant will undertake research, writing, development, consultation, and revision activities throughout the assignment.

Identify case studies and good practices

The consultant will research relevant case studies, examples, and good practices that can strengthen the toolkit.

These examples should help demonstrate how digital collective action works in different environments and what activists can learn from previous experiences.

The research should contribute to a toolkit that is grounded in practical experience rather than general theory alone.

Develop the Global Digital Action Toolkit

The consultant will write the approximately 15-page toolkit.

The publication is expected to address areas including:

Digital organising and protection

The toolkit should provide guidance on organising in digital environments while considering the safety, security, and resilience of participants.

Online mobilisation

The resource should explain practical approaches to mobilising people through digital platforms and building effective collective action online.

Responsible digital storytelling

The toolkit should address how activists and civil society organisations can use digital storytelling responsibly and strategically.

This may include considerations around how stories are collected, presented, communicated, and shared.

Strategic communications

The consultant should provide guidance on developing effective communications strategies for digital collective action.

This should help users communicate their objectives, reach relevant audiences, and strengthen their campaigns.

Impact measurement

The toolkit should provide practical approaches for understanding and measuring the impact of digital collective action.

This could help activists and organisations assess whether their digital campaigns are achieving their intended objectives and identify areas for improvement.

Expected Deliverables

The selected consultant will be expected to produce several key deliverables during the consultancy.

1. Inception Concept Note and Toolkit Outline

The first deliverable will establish the overall approach to the assignment.

It should include:

  • A proposed workplan
  • The methodology that will be used
  • The proposed structure of the toolkit
  • An outline of the proposed content
  • An approach to research and case-study identification

This stage will provide CIVICUS with an opportunity to review and provide direction before the full toolkit is developed.

2. First Draft

The consultant will prepare a complete first draft of the Global Digital Action Toolkit.

The draft will be submitted to the CIVICUS team for review and feedback.

It should demonstrate the proposed structure, content, practical recommendations, examples, and other relevant components of the final publication.

3. Final Toolkit

The final deliverable will be a publication-ready Global Digital Action Toolkit of approximately 15 pages.

The final version should incorporate feedback received from the CIVICUS team.

It should also include suggested:

  • Visuals
  • Graphics
  • References
  • Layout approaches
  • Other visual elements that could improve accessibility and usability

The consultant is therefore expected not only to provide written content but also to offer recommendations that can assist a visual designer in turning the material into an engaging final publication.

Consultancy Budget

CIVICUS has allocated a total budget of up to USD 9,000 for this consultancy.

The amount is inclusive of:

  • Professional fees
  • Taxes
  • Other associated costs

Applicants are required to submit a detailed financial proposal explaining their proposed consultancy fees and any anticipated expenses.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed budget clearly reflects the complete cost of delivering the assignment.

Consultancy Duration

The consultancy is expected to run for approximately three months.

The anticipated period is:

Mid-September to Mid-November 2026

Applicants should take this timeframe into consideration when developing their proposed methodology, workplan, and budget.

How to Apply

Interested consultants or consultancy teams should submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) by email to:FoPA@civicus.org

The email should use the following subject line: EOI – Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit

The application must be received by: 28 August 2026

Applicants are encouraged to ensure that all required documents are complete and submitted before the deadline.

Required Application Documents

The application should comprise three documents.

1. Full CV

Applicants should submit a full curriculum vitae outlining their professional background, relevant experience, qualifications, skills, and previous assignments.

The CV should clearly demonstrate experience relevant to the consultancy.

2. Cover Letter

The cover letter should be a maximum of two pages.

It should:

  • Introduce the applicant or consultancy team
  • Describe relevant skills and experience
  • Demonstrate understanding of the assignment
  • Explain the proposed approach
  • Describe how the assignment will be accomplished
  • Highlight experience that makes the applicant or team suitable for the work

Applicants should use the cover letter to demonstrate not only their qualifications but also their understanding of digital collective action and the needs of activists and civil society organisations.

3. Proposed Budget

Applicants must provide a proposed financial budget for undertaking the assignment.

The budget should clearly outline:

  • Consultancy fees
  • Anticipated expenses
  • Any other relevant costs

Since the maximum available budget is USD 9,000 inclusive of professional fees, taxes, and associated costs, applicants should ensure their proposal remains within the available budget.

What the Successful Consultant Will Be Expected to Deliver

The successful applicant will need to combine research, writing, strategic thinking, and an understanding of digital civic action.

The assignment requires more than simply producing a written report. The final resource should be a practical toolkit that activists and civil society organisations can actually use.

A strong approach would therefore need to consider:

  1. The realities of digital activism in different regions.
  2. The risks faced by activists using digital platforms.
  3. The opportunities created by online organising.
  4. Digital safety and resilience.
  5. Online mobilisation strategies.
  6. Responsible communications and storytelling.
  7. Strategic campaign communications.
  8. Methods for measuring digital campaign impact.
  9. Differences in political, legal, and technological environments.
  10. Accessibility and practical usability of the final toolkit.

Why This Consultancy Is Important

The increasing role of digital platforms in civic participation means that activists now need to understand both the opportunities and risks associated with digital collective action.

Digital spaces can help movements reach audiences that may be difficult to reach through traditional forms of organising. They can also facilitate rapid mobilisation, information sharing, storytelling, advocacy, and international solidarity.

At the same time, digital organising can expose activists and organisations to surveillance, misinformation, platform restrictions, online threats, and other challenges.

A practical Global Digital Action Toolkit can therefore help bridge the gap between traditional guidance on civic action and the realities of contemporary digital organising.

The resource will potentially provide activists and civil society organisations with practical knowledge that can be adapted to different contexts around the world.

Who Can Apply?

This opportunity is intended for qualified individual consultants or consultancy teams with relevant professional expertise and experience capable of researching and developing a global digital action resource.

Particularly relevant backgrounds may include:

  • Digital organising and activism
  • Civil society and civic-space work
  • Digital rights and digital security
  • Strategic communications
  • Advocacy and campaigning
  • Research and case-study development
  • Digital storytelling
  • Civil society capacity building
  • Development of toolkits, guides, publications, or similar resources

The Terms of Reference do not specify a particular nationality, race, ethnicity, or continent as an eligibility restriction. The assignment is designed for a global audience, and applicants should demonstrate the relevant expertise and experience required to successfully undertake the consultancy.

Interested applicants should nevertheless review the complete Terms of Reference and application requirements carefully before submitting their Expression of Interest.

Visit HERE to learn more about the

How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application

Applicants interested in this consultancy should ensure that their application directly responds to the requirements in the Terms of Reference.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate relevant experience rather than relying only on general professional qualifications.

Applicants can strengthen their submission by:

  • Clearly explaining previous experience with digital organising, civic action, communications, advocacy, activism, or civil society.
  • Providing relevant examples of research, publications, toolkits, guides, campaigns, or similar resources they have developed.
  • Demonstrating experience working with international or geographically diverse audiences.
  • Showing an understanding of digital safety and resilience.
  • Explaining their methodology for identifying credible case studies and good practices.
  • Presenting a realistic workplan for the three-month consultancy.
  • Providing a clear and detailed financial proposal.
  • Explaining how feedback from CIVICUS will be incorporated into subsequent drafts.
  • Demonstrating the ability to produce accessible and practical content.
  • Highlighting experience working with visual designers or preparing content that can easily be translated into visually engaging publications.

Important Dates and Application Information

Item Details
Organisation CIVICUS Global Alliance
Opportunity Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit
Opportunity type Consultancy
Budget Up to USD 9,000
Consultancy duration Approximately 3 months
Expected period Mid-September to mid-November 2026
Toolkit length Approximately 15 pages
Application method Expression of Interest by email
Application email FoPA@civicus.org
Email subject EOI – Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit
Application deadline 28 August 2026
Required documents Full CV, maximum two-page cover letter, proposed budget

Conclusion

The CIVICUS Global Digital Action Toolkit Consultancy 2026 presents an opportunity for an experienced consultant or consultancy team to contribute to an important global resource focused on digital civic action.

With a budget of up to USD 9,000, the assignment involves researching good practices, developing practical guidance, producing an approximately 15-page toolkit, incorporating feedback from CIVICUS, and delivering a publication-ready manuscript with recommendations for visuals and layout.

The consultancy is particularly relevant to professionals with experience in digital activism, civil society, civic space, advocacy, strategic communications, digital organising, research, digital rights, campaign development, or related fields.

Interested applicants should carefully prepare the three required application documents and submit their Expression of Interest to FoPA@civicus.org using the subject line “EOI – Development of the Global Digital Action Toolkit”.

The application deadline is 28 August 2026, with the consultancy expected to take place from mid-September to mid-November 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) is inviting aspiring economists to apply for its 2027 External Bursary Programme, designed to support prospective undergraduate students who intend to pursue studies in economics-related fields.

The bursary programme aims to help address skills shortages in South Africa by providing financial support to students from disadvantaged backgrounds who demonstrate strong academic potential and financial need.

Applications for the SARB Bursary Programme 2027 close on 30 September 2026.

About the SARB Bursary Programme

The South African Reserve Bank, through its Economic Research Department, in collaboration with the SARB Academy, provides external scholarships and bursaries to qualifying prospective undergraduate students each year.

The programme is particularly focused on supporting students who want to build careers in economics and related quantitative fields.

For the 2027 academic year, bursaries are available for students pursuing undergraduate degrees in:

  • Economics
  • Economics and Econometrics
  • Economics and Mathematical Statistics
  • Economic Science

The initiative forms part of SARB’s efforts to develop skills in areas that are important to South Africa’s economy and financial sector.

Who Is the SARB Bursary For?

The 2027 bursary is intended for prospective undergraduate students who will be entering their first year of university in 2027.

Applicants should already have or obtain provisional acceptance into an appropriate undergraduate degree programme in economics or one of the specified related fields.

The programme particularly seeks to support students who come from disadvantaged backgrounds and who demonstrate financial need.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the South African Reserve Bank Bursary 2027, applicants must meet the stated requirements.

1. Provisional University Acceptance

Applicants must have provisional acceptance into an undergraduate degree programme in an eligible economics-related field.

Proof of acceptance from a recognised institution must be provided as part of the application.

2. Academic Performance

Applicants must have achieved an average pass mark of at least 70% in their current year of study.

They must also demonstrate strong performance in:

  • English – 70% or above
  • Mathematics – 70% or above

Academic performance is an important part of the selection process because the bursary is intended to support students with strong potential to succeed in their chosen field.

3. Age Requirement

Applicants must be younger than 30 years of age.

4. Financial Need

Applicants must demonstrate financial need, meaning they are unable to afford university studies without financial assistance through a bursary.

The programme therefore provides an opportunity for academically capable students whose financial circumstances could otherwise prevent them from pursuing university education.

What Fields of Study Are Covered?

The SARB External Bursary Programme specifically identifies several eligible fields.

These include:

  1. Economics
  2. Economics and Econometrics
  3. Economics and Mathematical Statistics
  4. Economic Science

Students interested in careers related to economics, economic research, statistics, financial policy and related areas may therefore find this programme particularly relevant.

APPLY HERE

Documents Required

Applicants are required to provide supporting documentation with their applications.

The information provided for the programme indicates that applicants should submit:

  • Examination results
  • Proof of acceptance at a recognised institution
  • Student number
  • Any other relevant supporting documents

Applicants should ensure that their documentation is accurate and complete before submitting their application.

Incomplete or unsupported applications may affect the applicant’s ability to be considered.

SARB Bursary Application Promo Code

Applicants must use the following PROMO CODE when applying:

SARBERD27

Applicants should make sure that this code is correctly entered as part of their application.

How to Apply for the SARB Bursary 2027

Applicants have several options for submitting their applications.

Online Application

Applicants can apply online through the SARB bursary application platform:

https://sarb-bursary-manager.replit.app/

Email Application

Applications can also be submitted by email to:

sarbbursary@ttibursaries.co.za

Postal Application

Applicants who wish to submit their application by post can send it to:

Dimpho Nkoana
POSTNET Suite 101
Private Bag X153
Bryanston
2021
South Africa

Applicants should ensure that all required supporting documentation accompanies their application.

Visit HERE to learn more about the South African Reserve Bank Bursary 2027

Selection and Interviews

The SARB bursary is competitive, meaning that meeting the minimum requirements does not necessarily guarantee selection.

Potential external bursars may be required to attend an interview as part of the selection process.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to discuss their:

  • Academic background
  • Intended field of study
  • Career aspirations
  • Interest in economics
  • Financial circumstances
  • Motivation for applying for the bursary

Successful applicants will be expected to sign an agreement with the South African Reserve Bank.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the SARB External Bursary Programme 2027 is:

30 September 2026

Prospective applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline and ensure that all required documents have been included.

Why Apply for the SARB Bursary?

The programme provides an important opportunity for aspiring economists who have the academic ability to pursue university education but face financial barriers.

For eligible students, the opportunity can help them progress towards an undergraduate qualification in economics or a related quantitative discipline and potentially prepare for future careers in areas connected to economics and financial policy.

The programme is particularly relevant to students who:

  • Have a strong interest in economics
  • Perform well academically
  • Have strong English and Mathematics results
  • Plan to begin university in 2027
  • Require financial assistance to attend university
  • Want to develop a career in an economics-related field

Conclusion

The South African Reserve Bank Bursary Programme 2027 is an opportunity for prospective undergraduate students interested in economics and related fields to seek financial support for their university education.

The programme is aimed at students with strong academic performance, financial need and an interest in fields including Economics, Economics and Econometrics, Economics and Mathematical Statistics, and Economic Science.

Eligible applicants should obtain provisional acceptance into a recognised institution, prepare their academic and supporting documents, use the required promo code SARBERD27, and submit their applications before the 30 September 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
The NIHR School for Public Health Research (SPHR) has opened applications for its Transdisciplinary Fellowships (TDFs) in Public Health Research 2026, offering an opportunity for researchers working outside traditional public health disciplines to transition into public health research.

The fellowship is designed for researchers with strong research experience in areas such as engineering, architecture, law, public policy, arts and humanities, data science, and other relevant disciplines who want to apply their existing expertise to public health challenges.

Up to three fellowships are expected to be awarded. Successful fellows can undertake a fellowship of up to 24 months at one of the NIHR SPHR member institutions, develop their public health research expertise, complete a Public Health Master’s degree, work alongside established researchers, and prepare applications for future research funding.

Opportunity Category

Fellowship

What Is the NIHR SPHR Transdisciplinary Fellowship?

The NIHR School for Public Health Research’s Transdisciplinary Fellowship is intended to broaden the public health research workforce by bringing researchers from disciplines that are not traditionally viewed as pathways into public health research.

Public health challenges are complex and frequently require expertise extending beyond medicine and conventional health sciences. Issues such as health inequalities, mental health, urban environments, climate change, children’s wellbeing, social policy, technology and inclusion can benefit from knowledge and research approaches developed in other academic and professional fields.

The TDF programme therefore provides an opportunity for researchers from relevant non-traditional disciplines to combine their existing research expertise with public health research.

The fellowships will be based at one of the NIHR SPHR member institutions and can last for up to 24 months.

Key Highlights of the 2026 Fellowship

Applicants should take note of the following key details:

  • Opportunity: NIHR SPHR Transdisciplinary Fellowships in Public Health Research
  • Year: 2026
  • Fellowship duration: Up to 24 months
  • Expected number of awards: Up to three fellowships
  • Host: NIHR School for Public Health Research
  • Study requirement: Fellows are expected to complete a Public Health Master’s degree at their host SPHR member institution.
  • Research focus: Applied public health research aligned with one of the SPHR research programmes.
  • Target applicants: Researchers working outside disciplines traditionally associated with public health research.
  • Application status: Applications are currently open.
  • Deadline: 12:00 noon on Friday, 9 October 2026
  • International eligibility: Open to UK citizens and individuals with confirmed rights to work in the UK.
  • Future rounds: No further fellowship rounds are currently planned.

What Does the NIHR School for Public Health Research Do?

The NIHR School for Public Health Research (SPHR) brings together leading public health research expertise across England through a virtual research organisation.

Its broader objective is to strengthen the evidence available to support effective public health practice. The School conducts applied research designed to increase the volume and quality of evidence concerning interventions that can improve public health in cost-effective ways.

SPHR also works to support public health practitioners and policymakers in engaging with research and using evidence to inform decisions.

This makes the Transdisciplinary Fellowship particularly valuable for researchers who want to connect their existing disciplinary knowledge with real-world public health policy, practice and research.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship specifically targets people who are not currently working in traditional public health research disciplines, but whose academic or professional expertise has a meaningful connection to public health.

Examples of potentially relevant backgrounds include:

  • Engineering
  • Architecture
  • Law
  • Public policy
  • Data science
  • Arts and humanities
  • Other relevant disciplines outside conventional public health research

The programme recognises that public health is inherently transdisciplinary. Researchers can contribute to public health from a wide range of perspectives, methodologies and professional backgrounds.

For example, a data scientist could contribute advanced analytical approaches to public health research, while an architect could investigate how built environments influence health outcomes. Similarly, a public policy researcher could examine how government policies affect health inequalities.

Research Track Record Is Important

Applicants are expected to demonstrate a strong research track record in their base discipline.

The discipline in which the applicant has established their career or research expertise must have relevance to public health.

Applicants will need to provide evidence of research outputs appropriate to their particular field. The fellowship is therefore not simply aimed at individuals interested in changing careers; candidates are expected to demonstrate that they already have meaningful research experience and evidence of impact.

Research outputs may vary depending on the applicant’s discipline. What constitutes a strong research record in engineering, for example, may differ from what is expected in arts and humanities or data science.

Applicants should therefore present their research achievements in a way that clearly demonstrates:

  1. Their expertise in their existing discipline.
  2. Their ability to conduct high-quality research.
  3. The relevance of their work to public health.
  4. The impact or potential impact of their research.
  5. Their ability to contribute to transdisciplinary public health research.

Public Health Research Areas Covered by the Fellowship

The Transdisciplinary Fellowships will be aligned with the NIHR SPHR’s research programmes.

The four areas highlighted in the 2026 call are:

1. Health Inequalities

Health inequalities refer to differences in health outcomes and opportunities between different groups within society.

Research in this area can examine the social, economic, environmental, structural and policy factors that contribute to unequal health outcomes.

Researchers from non-traditional disciplines may bring valuable perspectives to understanding and addressing these inequalities.

2. Public Mental Health

Public mental health focuses on improving mental wellbeing and preventing mental health problems at population level.

The field can intersect with areas such as public policy, education, social sciences, technology, urban planning, communications, economics and community development.

3. Healthy Places, Healthy Planet

This programme considers the relationship between environments, places, planetary health and human wellbeing.

It provides significant opportunities for researchers from disciplines such as architecture, engineering, environmental studies, urban planning, data science and policy.

4. Children, Young People and Families

This research programme focuses on issues affecting children, young people and families.

Researchers from a variety of disciplines can contribute to understanding the factors that shape health and wellbeing during childhood, adolescence and family life.

What Will Successful Fellows Do?

Successful candidates will have the opportunity to work with established SPHR researchers to develop and shape research projects.

Rather than simply being placed into a predetermined project, fellows will have an opportunity to explore how their existing knowledge and expertise can complement ongoing research within the School.

This means the fellowship can serve as a bridge between the applicant’s original discipline and public health research.

The research project will be developed to align:

  • The fellow’s existing expertise.
  • Their research interests.
  • Their previous research experience.
  • Public health priorities.
  • The research expertise of SPHR researchers.
  • One or more of the School’s established research programmes.

Public Health Master’s Degree Requirement

One of the important features of this fellowship is that successful fellows are expected to complete a Public Health Master’s degree at their host SPHR member institution.

This requirement applies even to applicants who already hold a Master’s degree in another discipline.

Therefore, having an existing Master’s degree does not remove the requirement to undertake the Public Health Master’s associated with the fellowship.

The Master’s project must be aligned with the SPHR research programmes.

This component is particularly important because the fellowship is designed not only to provide research experience but also to help researchers build formal knowledge and skills in public health.

Can Applicants Who Already Have a Master’s Degree Apply?

Yes.

However, applicants who already hold a Master’s degree will still be expected to complete the relevant Public Health Master’s degree at their host member institution.

The existing Master’s degree does not substitute for the Public Health Master’s requirement.

Applicants should therefore consider whether they are prepared to undertake the additional academic component as part of the fellowship.

Who Is Not Eligible?

The fellowship is not intended for researchers who are already working in disciplines traditionally recognised as routes into public health research.

The call specifically identifies several disciplines and professions that are generally excluded.

These include:

  • Medicine
  • Epidemiology
  • Psychology
  • Sociology
  • Anthropology
  • Health economics
  • Medical statistics
  • Nursing
  • Dentistry
  • Physiotherapy
  • Nutrition
  • Other professions allied to medicine

This distinction is central to the purpose of the Transdisciplinary Fellowship.

The programme is designed to bring researchers from outside the conventional public health research pipeline into the field.

What If Your Background Is Non-Traditional but You Have Public Health Work Experience?

Applicants whose academic background is outside traditional public health disciplines but who already have some work experience in a public health-related field are advised to seek clarification before applying.

The programme does not provide an automatic yes-or-no answer for every possible combination of academic and professional experience.

If you fall into this category, you should contact the fellowship team at: sphr.training@ncl.ac.uk

Applicants are encouraged to clarify their eligibility before investing significant time in preparing an application.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is targeted at researchers who meet the following broad profile:

  • They work outside traditional public health research disciplines.
  • Their discipline has relevance to public health.
  • They have a strong research track record in their base discipline.
  • They can demonstrate relevant research outputs.
  • They can demonstrate the impact of their previous research.
  • They are interested in transitioning into or developing expertise in public health research.
  • They are eligible to work in the UK.
  • They are willing to undertake the required Public Health Master’s degree.
  • They are able to develop research aligned with one of the SPHR research programmes.

Countries and Nationalities Eligible to Apply

The fellowship is not open to applicants worldwide solely on the basis of nationality.

According to the fellowship information, applications are open to:

  • UK citizens
  • Individuals who have confirmed right to work in the UK

item.content:encoded:
The NATO South Caucasus Winter School for Young Leaders 2026 is now accepting applications from young people in Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan who are interested in NATO, international affairs, regional cooperation, and community engagement.

The five-day programme will bring together selected young professionals, students, and recent graduates for an educational experience focused on NATO’s mission, values, structure, history, and partnership with countries in the South Caucasus.

About the NATO South Caucasus Winter School 2026

The NATO South Caucasus Winter School for Young Leaders is designed to provide young participants with a deeper understanding of NATO and its engagement in the South Caucasus region.

The 2026 programme will take place from 30 November to 4 December 2026 in Lopota, Georgia.

Throughout the five-day programme, participants will have the opportunity to learn about NATO while engaging with topics relevant to the region. The programme will also include practical learning, including an exercise focused on countering disinformation.

What Participants Will Learn

The programme will focus on several important areas, including:

  • NATO’s mission and purpose
  • NATO’s core values
  • NATO’s structure and functioning
  • The history and development of NATO
  • NATO’s partnerships in the South Caucasus
  • Regional issues and cooperation
  • Countering disinformation
  • Ways young people can contribute to raising awareness about NATO within their communities

The practical exercise on countering disinformation is intended to give participants an opportunity to apply what they learn during the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The programme is specifically open to young people from Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

  • Be 18 to 25 years old
  • Be a student or recent graduate
  • Be from Georgia, Armenia, or Azerbaijan
  • Have a high level of English proficiency
  • Be able to participate in a programme conducted entirely in English
  • Demonstrate an interest in using the knowledge and experience gained through the Winter School within their communities

APPLY HERE

Participation Costs Are Covered

Selected participants will have their main programme-related costs covered by the organisers.

This includes:

  • Accommodation
  • Meals
  • Programme-related expenses

This makes the Winter School an accessible opportunity for eligible young people who want to participate in an international educational programme without having to cover the main costs associated with attendance.

Application Requirements

As part of the application process, applicants are required to submit a short video of no more than 90 seconds.

In the video, applicants should:

  1. Introduce themselves by stating their full name.
  2. State their country of origin.
  3. State the region they are originally from.
  4. Provide specific examples and plans explaining how they intend to use the knowledge and experience gained from the NATO South Caucasus Winter School 2026.
  5. Explain how they plan to raise awareness about NATO within their communities.

Applicants should use the video to communicate their own story, ideas, motivation, and plans clearly.

Important: AI Is Prohibited

The organisers have explicitly stated that the use of AI is strongly prohibited as part of the application process.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials, particularly the required video, represent their own ideas, experiences, voice, and personal perspective.

Programme Location and Dates

The Winter School will be held at:

Lopota, Georgia

Dates: 30 November – 4 December 2026

The programme will last five days.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply is:

31 August 2026 at 23:59

Applicants should ensure that their application and required video are submitted before the stated deadline.

Why Young People Should Consider This Opportunity

The NATO South Caucasus Winter School provides an opportunity for young participants to develop their understanding of an important international organisation and its relationship with the South Caucasus.

It can be particularly valuable for students and recent graduates interested in areas such as:

  • International relations
  • Diplomacy
  • International security
  • Political science
  • Regional affairs
  • Public policy
  • Youth leadership
  • Community engagement
  • Countering disinformation

Beyond learning about NATO, participants will also be expected to think about how they can take what they learn and use it to raise awareness within their own communities.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should complete the official application form and include the required 90-second video.

Before submitting, applicants should carefully check that their application:

  • Meets the age requirement
  • Is submitted by someone from an eligible country
  • Demonstrates a strong level of English
  • Includes the required personal information
  • Contains a video of no more than 90 seconds
  • Clearly explains how the applicant intends to use the programme’s knowledge and experience in their community

Applicants should also remember that AI use is strongly prohibited.

Visit HERE to learn more about the NATO South Caucasus Winter School for Young Leaders 2026

Conclusion

The NATO South Caucasus Winter School for Young Leaders 2026 offers students and recent graduates from Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan an opportunity to deepen their understanding of NATO, explore its partnerships in the South Caucasus, and develop practical knowledge around issues such as countering disinformation.

With accommodation, meals, and programme-related expenses covered, the five-day programme in Lopota, Georgia, provides an opportunity for young people to learn, engage and develop ideas for creating greater awareness about NATO within their communities.

Eligible applicants should prepare their applications and required 90-second video carefully and submit them by 31 August 2026 at 23:59.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
